Validated on the first draft and consistent with the computed answer (7548 MW, half-hour ending 18:30 AEST). Its supporting numbers are correct against the evidence and the store: 7448 MW in the half-hour containing the price peak (ending 18:00 AEST); the window's RRP peak of 121.12 $/MWh at 17:45 AEST; 0 intervals at the 300 $/MWh threshold. The hypotheses are hedged. The LILYSF1 non-conformance notice covers 12:40-12:45 AEST (56 MW), about six hours before the 18:30 peak, so the suggestion that it 'might be related to operational conditions around the window maximum' is weak (usefulness, not gated).

Consistent with the computed answer. The headline ("QLD1 highest operational demand: 7548.0 MW at 2026-07-29 18:30 AEST (interval end)") and summary ("The window maximum operational demand was 7548.0 MW at 2026-07-29 18:30 AEST") agree with it. The supporting figures check out: 7448.0 MW for the half-hour ending 08:00Z (ev0036, L78), which does contain the 5-minute RRP interval ending 07:45Z (ev0687, $121.12/MWh), and 0 intervals at or above $300 (ev0916). Weak point: "The AEMO non-conformance notice for QLD1 about unit LILYSF1 [c1] might be related to operational conditions around the window maximum" is hedged but poorly supported. The cited notice (market_notice_144689) gives "Duration: 29/07/2026 12:40 to 29/07/2026 12:45", a 5-minute, 56 MW solar-unit event about six hours before the 18:30 peak, so it is not 'around' the maximum. The weather hypothesis is hedged and flagged as untested. "This report does not assert causation" keeps both from being causal claims stated as fact.

Weak points: (1) the headline "Reported QLD1 operational demand at 2025-10-05 00:30 AEST ...: 5693.0 MW" does not itself say 'not established', but it does not call the value a maximum either; (2) the possible explanation "This observed maximum might not be the full local-day peak" uses 'maximum' loosely but hedges it at once; (3) "The reported operational-demand value might reflect the reconstituted actual operational demand that includes estimated Wholesale Demand Response" is hedged but sits poorly with ev0001's definition ("Average 30-minute measured operational demand MW value (unadjusted)") and with the cited passage (aemo_demand_terms#p10c15), which says the WDR estimate is a separate field; (4) the forecast/MAE material (targets 2025-10-04T20:00Z..2025-10-05T08:00Z) was not asked for. It is accurately reported as unavailable, but it is padding.

interpretation_notes: Validated after one repair. Every gold item is right and consistent with the evidence: the run issued 2026-08-19T21:57:01Z, the last before the half-hour; POE10/50/90 of 1663/1594/1525 MW and an actual of 1567 MW for the half-hour ending 08:00 ACST; an error of 27.0 MW (1.72%). Usefulness is reduced by summary item 3 (below) and the leaked internal field name 'forecast_mae_evidence_id'.

The asked-for facts are right and clearly stated. The run is PUBLIC_FORECAST_OPERATIONAL_DEMAND_HH_202608200830_20260820080131, "issued 2026-08-19T21:57:01Z" (the last run issued before the half-hour began at 22:00Z). Values: "POE10 = 1663.0 MW, POE50 = 1594.0 MW, POE90 = 1525.0 MW for target end 2026-08-20 08:00 ACST" and actual "1567.0 MW". The error "27.0 MW, i.e. 1.72%" matches ev0552 and ev0553. The explanations are hedged ("may reflect", "might reflect") and the answer admits no PV or weather data were retrieved. Problems: (1) "The run/actual pair for the review yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of 149.81 MW (see forecast_mae_evidence_id)" comes straight after the 27 MW single-interval error. It reads as the error of the asked-for pair, but it is ev0676's mean |error| over 21 of 24 half-hours (2026-08-19T22:30Z..2026-08-20T08:30Z, 08:00-18:00 ACST), whose coverage is marked incomplete; neither its window nor its incompleteness is stated, and it points the reader to an internal field name. (2) "The document search record indicates one market notice is held for this region and window" cannot be traced to any evidence item. Also, the sheet's 'interpretation' field reads "unknown", while the label says "checked by the independent validator" and validation says "passed after one repair". I treated the interpretation as validated.
